problems.title: Reported metric triples need their aggregation reconciled
problems.source_location: Tables 1, 5 and 6; Appendix D.2 and D.7
claim: The paper describes ordinary information-extraction F1, precision and recall, but does not fully specify column populations, weights or undefined-case treatment.
analysis: For ordinary per-unit F1 \(h(p,r)=2pr/(p+r)\), the Hessian quadratic form is \(-4(ra-pb)^2/(p+r)^3\le0\). Thus common nonnegative weights imply \(\bar F\le h(\bar P,\bar R)\), including hierarchical common-weight macro averages. Table 1 reports AutoAgent–Stock \((F,P,R)=(73.54,94.37,52.71)\) percent. Even two-decimal rounding requires \(73.535\le h(94.375,52.715)=67.64536\), impossible. However different column weights or populations can violate that necessary bound without an arithmetic error. Mere inequality between macro F1 and the harmonic mean is not itself a defect.
result: The row is inconsistent under a common-weight interpretation, but the actual aggregation remains unresolved. No replacement F1 or changed method ranking follows without scoring code and per-unit data.
problems.impact_rationale: The decisive inequality is conditional on an unspecified aggregation convention, preventing an unconditional paper-error classification.
